epic.title: WPP at Scale
epic.overview: Take the operational learnings from the first WPP pilot market and build them into the platform so the remaining WPP markets are easier to run than the first, with each feature designed to serve more than just WPP where possible.

milestones.title: M1 — Core Operational Efficiency
milestones.overview: The foundational bulk-management and monitoring tools research leads need to run large WPP projects day to day: survey compatibility, bulk survey actions, external panels, targeting bucket filtering, automated field reporting and WPP dashboard.

milestones.title: M2 — Expansion & Follow-On Builds
milestones.overview: Real-Time Survey Translation and Quota Management Between Cells require further conversation before build. Externalise Hardcoded Script Values is ready to build but was grouped here to keep M1 focused.

milestones.title: M3 — WPP API Platform
milestones.overview: Stand up fieldwork-api — a new, separately hosted serverless API (AWS Lambda/TypeScript, own repo) that (a) provides the data layer for the WPP Dashboard (F1.6) and (b) takes ownership of everything currently served by src/routes/wpp in dashboard-api (/wpp, /wpp/exports, /wppMonitoring), restructured for the ~470-cell multi-market scale of 2026-W1.

milestones.title: M4- WPP Dashboard
milestones.overview: Provide WPP with a dashboard showing how markets are progressing — a single up-to-date view of market progress without manual reporting. The dashboard is a static web app reading the hourly per-market MetricsSnapshot JSON from S3 (produced by M3 / F3.3); it does not read the database directly and has no backend of its own.

features.title: F1.1 — Excel Template & Survey Compatibility
features.overview: Validate the survey template against the demographic questions in the questions Excel before survey creation, to ensure the survey structure will be compatible with downstream coding and data delivery processes. Only demographic questions are validated at this stage, since other questions and options may be populated after creation (e.g., assigned to users later). This prevents launching surveys with mismatched demographic questions, options, or response values that could lead to incorrect data processing later.
features.rationale: Product signed this off as Done; two of five stories have merged PRs on master while the other three show done-unverified because their own PRs closed unmerged, though the same validation logic landed via the later merged end-to-end PRs.

features.title: F3.3 — Dashboard Metrics
features.overview:
Deliver the data layer for the WPP fieldwork dashboard (F1.6): an hourly per-market metrics snapshot produced inside the fieldwork-processing Step Functions workflow (EventBridge hourly start → discover → fail-closed QC gate → per-market metrics compute → S3). Each successful cycle writes a validated, aggregate-only MetricsSnapshot JSON to a dedicated snapshot bucket:

There is no HTTP API in v1 (design change 2026-08-05): the previously planned /v1/dashboard/* endpoints, ?fresh=true recompute, OpenAPI client codegen, and per-market SQS fan-out are all gone. The dashboard reads the snapshot JSON directly from S3; the embedded computedAt is the UI's "last sync" indicator. There is no per-request recompute path.

v1 is scoped to data we already capture: completes vs target, starts/in-progress/IR%, screen-out breakdown, per-QC-check counts, research-defender counts, quota-cell fill, LOI (average/median/per-section), daily completes, grade/region tallies, and per-cell drill-down data. Derived values (percentages, deltas, totals) are deliberately not stored — consumers compute them. Forecast/RAG/Fount go-live metrics are v2, blocked on WPP supplying field dates.
features.rationale: Eleven of fifteen stories are shipped with merged PRs across fieldwork-processing and fieldwork-dashboard covering discovery, metrics compute, and QC porting; the remaining QC-worker port has PRs still open for review and two stories haven't started, so this is well underway but not finished.

acCoverage.label: Dashboard reads one small per-market snapshot instead of fanning out to Firestore
A failed compute preserves the last-known-good snapshot, badged stale, with an age alarm
Conditional writes stop a delayed/duplicate run from overwriting a newer snapshot
Snapshot validates against a versioned, aggregate-only schema with no PII
A QC failure fails the workflow closed, leaving metrics uncomputed and the snapshot untouched

features.title: F4.1 — Dashboard
features.overview: Build the static WPP fieldwork dashboard app: a rebuild matching the WPP BAV “Fieldwork Command Centre” prototype design (share link — a design guide, not a contract; we do not reuse its source), consuming the per-market MetricsSnapshot JSON produced by fieldwork-processing (F3.3 / BOUN-11442). No backend: the page reads S3-served JSON only.
features.rationale: The single story is shipped with a merged PR whose files match nearly every AC block (market overview, quota meters, daily completes, derived values, demo-QC tests), though product sign-off is not recorded for this ticket.

acCoverage.label: Static app is typed against the versioned snapshot schema with a clear update-required state for unknown versions
Clean, minimal UI with bold labels/emphasis
App polls the per-market snapshot roughly every 60s with no recompute or direct Firestore access
Market overview renders all v1 content blocks
Derived values are computed client-side, not stored
Works against demo-QC snapshots for UI development
Derived-value logic and components are covered by tests against a fixture snapshot

features.title: F4.2 — Dashboard hosting, CDN & access control
features.overview: Serve the dashboard and the snapshot JSON from one place, and decide + implement who can see it. This resolves the M3 plan's open question (“public-read vs CloudFront vs signed access to the snapshot bucket”) and step-functions.md open question 4 (cache policy/CDN between the private snapshot bucket and the HTML page).
features.rationale: No work has started — the single story is still todo with zero PRs.

acCoverage.label: Dashboard assets and snapshot JSON are served from one private, CloudFront-fronted origin
Cache policy gives long-lived caching for assets and near-real-time revalidation for latest.json
Access control is decided and implemented for WPP stakeholders only
Terraform owns the stateful infra per the house split
A runbook documents cache invalidation and freshness verification

features.title: F4.3 — Per-cell drill-down views
features.overview: Per-study/per-cell drill-down within each market, mirroring today's #wpp-bav-uk-market reporting so internal researchers can spot problem cells without running exports.
features.rationale: No work has started — the single story is still todo with zero PRs.

acCoverage.label: Drill-down opens from the market overview using the same snapshot, no extra requests
Drill-down shows the cell's funnel, quota fill, grade/region, QC counts and LOI
Cells needing attention are visually flagged against agreed thresholds
Drill-down is deep-linkable by market + cell
Component tests are driven by the shared fixture snapshot

stories.summary: F4.3 — Per-cell drill-down views

features.title: F4.4 — Staleness badging & data-status UX
features.overview: Make data trustworthiness visible: users should always know how fresh the numbers are, when they're degraded, and which panels aren't real yet. This is the UI half of the pipeline's staleness contract (markStale in MetricsSnapshotS3Store).
features.rationale: No work has started — the single story is still todo with zero PRs.

acCoverage.label: computedAt renders as a visible last-sync timestamp everywhere
A stale:true snapshot shows a degraded-data banner without blanking the page
A snapshot older than 3 cycles shows the same degraded banner client-side even without a stale flag
Date-derived v2 panels stay hidden until field dates exist
QC panels are marked as demo data while QC_DATA_MODE=demo
A failed poll keeps last-rendered data with a connection-lost indicator
Each staleness state has its own component test
